text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- Parliament is set to start debating a bill on nuclear energy this week and is due to begin debating the 1997 budget bill Monday, if the cabinet submits it, said deputy speaker Agnes Maczo. @

- The Young Democrats' governing board yesterday demanded that Industry and Trade Minister Tamas Suchman be dismissed over what it claimed was an unjustified payment of fees by the State Privatisation and Holding Co. to a lawyer.
- The World Bank will extend a $225 million 12-year loan to support the restructuring of Hungary's corporate and banking sectors. (Sat.)
- Japan's Eximbank will provide a loan of 5 billion yen to Hungary under the first credit agreement it has signed with Hungary's Export-Import Bank. @
- Apple producers will receive a state subsidy of HUF 590 million.
- Top officials of General Motors along with Hungarian President Arpad Goncz opened Opel Hungary's new cylinderhead manufacturing plant in Szentgotthard on Friday. (Sat.)
NEPSZABADSAG

- Ferenc Somogyi, head of the Foreign Ministry's state secretariat for integration, said that negotiations on admission to the EU could be wound up around 2000 and Hungary cannot expect full membership before 2002. @
- Diplomatic sources in Brussels said Hungary would in all probability receive an invitation to join NATO in the spring of 1997 and Hungary has every chance of gaining full membership in 1999.
- The Hungarian IFOR contingent together with Italian NATO soldiers have repaired a 65-km stretch of railway in Serbia.

- The Swiss paper Neue Zurcher Zeitung wrote in its weekend edition that the 1997 draft budget approved by the Hungarian cabinet not only continues the March 1995 austerity programme but aims to give an impetus to economic growth.
MAGYAR HIRLAP @
- The Tax Authority will open 130 new taxpayer service offices across the country in the coming weeks and plans to expand its staff by 1,800-2,400 by early next year. (Sat.)
- In a full-page interview, Sandor Lezsak, president of the Democratic Forum reveals internal conflicts that marred the Antall administration. (Sat.)
- The border station between Udvar and Nezevo, Croatia, is due to be re-opened on October 4 after a nearly five-year interruption.
- A report details micro-business growth in Hungary during the first seven months of the year. @
- The weekend ban on trucks heavier than 3.5 tonnes will continue to be in effect from January 1 next year.
NAPI GAZDASAG
- Top government officials will meet representatives of the foreign owners of several energy companies today.
- The BUX Index basket takes in four new member-shares as of today.
VILAGGAZDASAG @
- The EBRD announced on Friday its willingness to allow the disclosure of contracts it signed in the privatisation of Budapest Bank, including secret clauses, joining the other owner, GE Capital.
- A domestic consortium led by the Hungarian State Railways aims to establish a major new telecommunications company in January 1997 which it hopes could become a competitor to Matav by 2002.
